title: Robust HRV dispersion: the interquartile range (a new op) reproduces scipy AND base R bit-for-bit -- and exposes a skewed RR distribution

dataset.name: Fantasia database
dataset.record: subject f1y01 (young healthy adult), first 5-minute RR-interval window (391 intervals, ms)
dataset.citation: Iyengar N, Peng CK, Morin R, Goldberger AL, Lipsitz LA. Age-related alterations in the fractal scaling of cardiac interbeat interval dynamics. Am J Physiol 1996;271:R1078-R1084. Fantasia database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: SDNN, the standard deviation of the RR intervals, is the classical HRV dispersion but is inflated by the ectopic beats and large respiratory excursions that make the RR distribution non-Gaussian. The interquartile range is the robust, quantile-based alternative. The ecosystem had the classical SD (signalMoments) and a deviation-based robust scale (medianAbsDev) but no quantile-based robust spread. This case introduces interquartileRange. On real Fantasia RR intervals it reproduces BOTH scipy.stats.iqr AND base R IQR BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| 0 vs each). The finding: the RR distribution is right-skewed and heavy-tailed (skewness 1.01, excess kurtosis 2.91), so the robust IQR-based SD estimate (56.3 ms) sits materially below SDNN (69.3 ms; ratio 0.81) -- the opposite of the near-Gaussian EEG (median-abs-dev case), where the robust scale matched the SD. The robust/classical ratio is a distribution-shape diagnostic.

claims.statement: interquartile range of the RR intervals (robust HRV dispersion)
first quartile (25th percentile) of the RR intervals
third quartile (75th percentile) of the RR intervals
SDNN (classical SD of the RR intervals) for the robust-vs-classical comparison
robust IQR-based SD / SDNN -- below 1 for a heavy-tailed distribution
skewness of the RR distribution (non-Gaussian, right-skewed)

validation.reference: The new interquartileRange op is validated against BOTH scipy.stats.iqr AND base R IQR on the identical RR vector (both type-7 quantiles) -- a double reference. All three compute IQR = Q3 - Q1 and agree BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| 0 vs each). SDNN, the robust IQR-based SD estimate, their ratio, and the RR skewness are reported for the robust-vs-classical comparison.
validation.data: REAL -- Fantasia (PhysioNet), subject f1y01, first 5-minute RR window (391 intervals)
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the new interquartileRange op reproduces scipy and base R bit-for-bit; (2) the robust IQR-based spread is well below SDNN on this skewed RR distribution. HONEST scope: (1) this is a NEW quantile-based robust-dispersion op, completing the robust toolkit alongside medianAbsDev (deviation-based scale) and signalMoments (classical SD); the ecosystem had no quantile-based robust spread; (2) with the default type-7 quantiles it reproduces BOTH scipy.stats.iqr (linear interpolation) AND base R IQR BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| = 0 vs each) -- a genuine DOUBLE-REFERENCE machine-precision agreement, because Q3 and Q1 are unambiguous ORDER STATISTICs under the shared convention, NOT A CONVENTION AGREEMENT; (3) the finding, and why it matters for HRV: on the Fantasia RR intervals the distribution is right-SKEWED and heavy-tailed (skewness 1.01, excess kurtosis 2.91), so the robust IQR-based SD estimate IQR/(2*qnorm(0.75)) = 56.3 ms sits materially below SDNN = 69.3 ms (ratio 0.81); the robust/classical dispersion ratio is thus a DISTRIBUTION-SHAPE DIAGNOSTIC, and here it shows SDNN IS INFLATED by the heavy right tail (long RR intervals from respiratory sinus arrhythmia and occasional ectopy) that the robust IQR ignores; (4) this is the OPPOSITE of the NEAR-GAUSSIAN eyes-closed EEG in the MEDIAN-ABS-DEV case, where the robust scale matched the SD to 0.2% (ratio 1.002); (5) IQR itself (76 ms) is a legitimate robust HRV dispersion index, resistant to the ectopic beats that corrupt SDNN; (6) the value is a property of one subject/window; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: Because the robust/classical dispersion ratio (robust IQR-scale over SDNN) drops below 1 exactly when the RR distribution departs from Gaussian, it is a cheap non-normality / artifact flag for HRV: a ratio well below 1 signals that SDNN is being driven by a heavy tail (ectopy or large respiratory excursions) rather than uniform beat-to-beat variability. Pairing IQR with SDNN, or robust-cleaning the RR series before SDNN, would separate the two. Documented, not escalated.
